Hi Aisha / Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Long story short — BrightGrid can commit to a substantial monthly usage profile if we can get a meaningful concession on per-token rates. Our procurement team is asking whether Redwood can offer something nearer $0.00020/token (roughly 50% off your published rate card) once we scale above ~5B tokens/month.

Attached is our Q2 forecast and a simple cadence showing when we expect to ramp. Procurement (Tom) is looped in on this email. Can you let us know whether Redwood has flexibility on per-token pricing or whether a committed tier/ladder would be the right approach? Ideally we need a response within 72 hours to keep internal momentum.

Thanks,
Pooja Reddy
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightGrid

Date: 2027-03-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightGrid committed pricing request - need pricing exception / committee input

Aisha / Marissa — forwarding BrightGrid's ask. Key points:
- Customer willing to commit materially (they model 4–6B tokens/month by month 3).
- Asking for ~50% off rate card (target $0.00020/token).
- Procurement (Tom) needs a fit-for-contract number to take to legal/finance.

My read: this is a large strategic account if we hold product SLAs and can protect margin via minimum guarantees and overruns. Proposed internal options:
1) Offer a 12-month committed tier with a guaranteed minimum of 3B tokens/month and stepped per-token pricing:
   - 0–3B: $0.00045/token (baseline commitment rate)
   - 3B–6B: $0.00028/token (~30% off)
   - >6B: $0.00022/token (conditional rebate after performance)
2) Or keep published rate-card but add a volume rebate at quarter close, up to 50% effective discount if they hit corridors.

Risks: margin compression and precedent for other customers asking for similar concessions. Suggest approvals required: Marissa sign-off for manager-level concession and finance (Aditya) to confirm margin and rebate mechanics. Legal will want strict commit/recoup language.

Attaching the forecast and the counterparty redlines they've hinted at. If we can get a thumbs up for the above framework (or a straight 30% cap), I'll draft a one-page term sheet and a HubSpot update (opp 95832).

—Karthik

Thanks for the context, Karthik. I reviewed the numbers and the strategic upside here is real — this could become a multi-region anchor account. That said, we need to protect unit economics. I'm comfortable approving a controlled exception with the following constraints:

- Approval: up to 30% off our published per-token rate for a 12-month committed program, contingent on a minimum guaranteed usage of 3B tokens/month.
- Mechanic: implement a tiered committed rate (0–3B / 3B–6B / >6B) where the 3B–6B band gets ~30% off. Any effective discount beyond that (toward 50%) must be delivered via a retroactive quarterly rebate tied to performance triggers and limited recoup if commit not met.
- Conditions: finance (Aditya) to confirm acceptable margin impact and rebate escrow mechanics; legal to insert recoup and audit rights; commit to a 30-day term-sheet expiry and a 10-day signature window after counters.
- No precedence clause: include explicit language limiting this exception to BrightGrid deal ID BG-2027-045.

Aditya — please confirm margin runway and whether we can operationalize a quarterly rebate/escrow. If finance greenlights, I'll ask Legal to prepare the term sheet language and give a go/no-go to present to BrightGrid.

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal: BrightGrid committed pricing & next steps (BG-2027-045)

Hi Pooja / Tom — thanks for the patience. Internal alignment is done; below is the proposal we can take to your procurement/legal teams.

Summary (high level)
- Commitment: 12 months starting on the Effective Date with a minimum guaranteed volume of 3B tokens/month.
- Pricing (committed tier):
  • 0–3B tokens/month: $0.00045/token
  • 3B–6B tokens/month: $0.00028/token (manager-approved concession ~30% off list)
  • >6B tokens/month: $0.00022/token (requires performance triggers; implemented as quarterly rebate up to this effective price if corridor met)
- Payment & rebate mechanics: quarterly true-up with rebate held in escrow; recoup if commit not met in the following quarter (standard clawback language).
- Term: 12 months with a 10-day signature window for this term sheet.

Next steps
1) If this framework looks acceptable, I'll share a 1–2 page term sheet and a DocuSign link for signatures.
2) Legal will include explicit non-precedence language limiting the exception to BG-2027-045.
3) Procurement to confirm billing cadence and PO timing; we can align on onboarding dates after signature.

Attachments: BrightGrid_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet draft), BrightGrid_Q2_forecast.xlsx
HubSpot opp: HS:opp_95832
